# Operation semantics

What the operations a C compiler emits actually compute: operand order,
inverted forms, extension, out-of-range shift counts, division corner
cases, compare predicates, NaN handling. [bundle.md](bundle.md) and
`binutils-ops.yaml` give encodings and channels; this page gives the
behaviour.

Status: **[hw]** observed on an Elbrus 4C (elbrus-v3) by
`tools/isa-probes/semantics.c` (wrappers generated by
`gen_semantics.py`; one generic v3 binary prints the same 308 lines on
the 4C, the Elbrus-8C2 and the 2C3 apart from `%idr`, the machine's
identification, which also varies between runs on one machine);
**[guide]** from the MCST programming guide, chapter
10, and for v5 operations on an Elbrus-8C2 by `sem5.c` (section "v5
operations"). MCST's qemu agrees with the hardware on every case it
can run except the quiet FP compares below (`semantics.c emu` skips the cases
that trap, at which it aborts: "exception handling is
unimplemented").
Latencies are in [timing.md](timing.md).

32-bit (`...s`) operations below were run under `setwd dbl = 0`: they
write the low half of the destination and keep the upper half
([registers.md](../abi/registers.md), `dbl`).

## Integer arithmetic and logic [hw]

| Operation | Result |
|---|---|
| `subd a, b, dst` | a − b. (`rsub` exists only as the second stage of combined operations.) |
| `andnd a, b, dst` | a & ~b (the **second** operand is inverted) |
| `ornd a, b, dst` | a \| ~b |
| `xornd a, b, dst` | a ^ ~b |
| `merged a, b, dst, pred` | **a when pred is false**, b when true: the reverse of `pred ? a : b`. `~%predN` is accepted. `merges` alike (both model-checked by `tagx.c`, "Other scalar operations") |
| `sxt n, src, dst` | n = 0, 1, 2: sign-extend 8, 16, 32 bits; n = 4, 5, 6: **zero**-extend 8, 16, 32 bits; 3 = 2, 7 = 6. The guide (10.3.8) has the sign bit the other way round; lcc emits `sxt 0x1` for `short`, `0x5` for `unsigned short` |
| `smulhd a, b`, `umulhd a, b` | high 64 bits of the signed / unsigned 128-bit product |
| `popcntd`, `popcnts` | number of set bits |
| `lzcntd`, `lzcnts` | leading zeros; 64 (32) for zero |
| `bitrevd`, `bitrevs` | bit reversal |

There are no 64-bit or 32-bit remainder operations: compute a % b as
a − (a / b) × b. (`smodx`/`umodx` give the remainder of a 64-bit by
32-bit division only, below.)

## Shifts and rotates [hw]

`shl`, `shr` (logical), `sar` (arithmetic), `scl`, `scr` (rotate left,
right), each in `s` (32-bit) and `d` (64-bit) forms. The count is taken
**modulo the operand width**: `shld` by 64 or 128 returns the operand
unchanged, by 65 shifts by 1; `shls` by 32 returns it unchanged. Only the
low bits of the count register matter: `shls` ignores the count's upper
32 bits (a count of `0xaaaaaaaa00000001` shifts by 1), `shld` by
`0xffffffffffffffff` shifts by 63. For GCC: `SHIFT_COUNT_TRUNCATED` holds.

## Field extract: `getf` [hw]

`getfd src1, src2, dst` (`getfs` for 32 bits) **rotates src1 right by
an offset and keeps the low *len* bits, zero- or sign-extended**, with
the field described by src2, usually a literal. It runs in all six ALU
channels with latency 1 (timing.md), so one operation does what takes
a shift and an `and` (or two shifts) elsewhere:

| src2 bits (`getfd`; `getfs`) | Field |
|---|---|
| 0–5; 0–4 | offset: src1 is rotated right by it |
| 6–11; 6–10 | *len*, the bits kept (0–63; 0–31) |
| 12 | 1: sign-extend from the field's top bit; 0: zero-extend |
| 13–15 | v1–v4: BYTE, which byte holds the sign bit (below; `getfd` 13–15, `getfs` 13–14); v5+: ignored by `getf`; bits 13–15 are the low-zero count of `getfzd` and `getfzs` |
| 16 and up | ignored |

A constant descriptor with *len* ≥ 1 is at least 64, above the free
4-bit `src2` literal (0–15), so a field operation with a constant field
(`getf*`, `getfz*`, `insf*`) always takes a literal: half an LTS as a
16-bit one, a whole LTS where lcc writes one with bit 15 set as 32-bit
(below; [bundle.md](bundle.md), "Literal values") [checked: gas].

`tools/isa-probes/getf.c` runs every offset, length, sign bit and BYTE
value with five values of src1 (368,640 cases a machine) against the
community qemu's two helpers, and the 4C follows its v1 rule, the
Elbrus-8C2 its v5 rule, in every case; the 2C3 follows the v5 rule too
(327,680 `getfd` and 40,960 `getfs` cases, none differing from the v5
model):

- **The sign bit.** v5 sign-extends from the field's top bit, bit
  (offset + *len* − 1) mod width of src1. v1–v4 take it from bit
  8 × BYTE + ((offset + *len* − 1) & 7) of src1, so the descriptor
  must name the byte: **with BYTE = ((offset + *len* − 1) mod width) /
  8 the two rules agree**, and that descriptor is right on every
  version (lcc always builds it so: `(long) (x << 40) >> 50` is
  `getfd x, 0x538a`, offset 10, *len* 14, BYTE 2). A wrong BYTE on v3
  gives the sign of an unrelated bit.
- ***len* 0** keeps no bits but still extends: 0 without bit 12, and
  with it all ones or 0 by the bit just below the field (bit
  offset − 1, on v1–v4 through BYTE as above).
- Fields wrap: a field that runs past the top continues at bit 0 (it
  is a rotate). `getfs` writes 32 bits (under `setwd dbl = 0` the upper
  half is kept).
- With a register descriptor, `getfd x, n << 6` is `x & ((1 << n) − 1)`
  for every n from 0 to 63, and `getfd x, k | n << 6` is
  `(x >> k) & ((1 << n) − 1)` for k + n ≤ 64.

`getfzd`/`getfzs` (v5+) are `getf` that then clears the result's low
BYTE bits (0–7) [community qemu `helper_int.c`; matches the 8C2 in
`sem5.c`]: a contiguous mask that doesn't start at bit 0, such as
`(x >> 8) & 0xff0` (offset 8, *len* 12, 4 zero bits), is one operation.
`getf` is also the first stage of the combined `getf_and*` … `getf_xorn*`,
`getf_add*`, `getf_sub*` (ALC1/4; "Combined operations", below).

What lcc emits at `-O3` (v3 and v5 alike; v5 adds `getfz` for fields
shifted left, below): `(x >> 20) & 0x7f` → `getfd
x, 0x1d4`; `(x >> 37) & 1` → `getfd x, 0x65`; sign-extending shifts
`(long) (x << 52) >> 52` → `getfd x, 0x3300`; bit-field reads
(`s.b`, a signed 22-bit field at bit 13: `getfd w, 0x958d`, a 32-bit
literal because BYTE 4 sets bit 15, though a negative 16-bit one would
do: below); `x >> k` and `x & 0xfff` stay
`shrd` and `andd`. On 32-bit values it uses `getfs` where the field
stays 32-bit (inside a computation, CoreMark's `crcu16`), and `getfd`
only on a whole 64-bit register: after `sxt 6` (zero-extension) under
`dbl = 0`, after a load, or on a result that `dbl = 1` zero-extended
(`((x ^ y) >> 3) & 0x1ff` returned: `setwd dbl = 1`, `xors`, `getfd`)
[lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`, v3 and v5]. So it never reads a 32-bit result's
upper half, which under `dbl = 0` arrives 4 cycles after the producer
instead of 1 (timing.md, "Formats") and may be diagnostic.

**`getfz` in lcc's v5 code.** lcc emits `getfzd`/`getfzs` where the
source shifts a field left by 1 to 7 bits, written as a shift, a
multiply or an array index, and not where the same value is written as
a mask with its zeros (below) [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3` for v5.8c2 and
v6.2c3, lcc 1.31.05 for v5.8c2; `tools/isa-probes/foldisa_getfz.c`]:

| Source | lcc's code (1.29.16, v5.8c2 and v6.2c3) |
|---|---|
| `((x >> 7) & 0xff) << 4`, its `* 16` form, `p[(i >> 7) & 0xff]` with 16-byte elements | `getfzd x, 0x8303` (offset 3, *len* 12, 4 zero bits); v3: `shrd x, 3` + `andd 0xff0` |
| the same index with 2-, 4- or 8-byte elements | `getfzd` with 1–3 zero bits |
| a bit-field shifted left; a signed field shifted left, `((x << 40) >> 50) << 3` | one `getfzd`; `getfzd x, 0x7447` (bit 12 set, v5's sign rule) |
| a 32-bit field shifted left | one `getfzs` |
| a 32-bit index | `sxt 6` (zero-extension) first, as for `getfd` |
| a field at bit 0 shifted left: `(x & 0xfff) << 4`, `t[x & 0xff]`, `t[(unsigned char) x]` | mostly two operations: `andd` or `sxt 4`, then `shld` |
| a byte that an inline function uses as a table index, as in glibc's `strcasecmp` for E2K (`ch1 = (a0) & 0xff; TOLOWER (ch1)`) | `getfzd a0, 0x42be` (offset 62, the field wrapping round to bit 0, 2 zero bits) |
| `t[(unsigned char) (x >> 8)]` | `shrd`, `sxt 4` and `shld`; lcc 1.31.05: `getfzd x, 0x4286` |
| a field shifted left by 8 or more: `((x >> 16) & 0xff) << 8` | `shrd` + `andd`: no single `getfz`, as the 3-bit count allows 7 zeros at most |

So `getfz` sits where indexes are scaled. Lua 5.4.7 built so for
v5.8c2 has 189, 174 of them in `luaV_execute` (mostly the
instruction's 8-bit A, B and C fields times 16, a `TValue`: `getfzd i,
0x8303`, A × 16, 83 times there and 87 in all; also A and B times 8 and
the Bx and Ax fields times 4, 8 or 16) and four `getfzs i, 0xe3c9` in
`lcode.c` that move the B field (bits 16–23) to A's place (bits 7–14),
two of them with the descriptor in a register [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`,
v5.8c2]; lcc's v5 libraries have 1,192 (`lcc-usage.yaml`), among them
libc's `_des_crypt` 384 (each with a register descriptor),
`__strncasecmp_nonascii` 98 and `__strcasecmp_nonascii` 68 and
libcrypt's `__init_des_r` 248, `setkey_r` 225 (169 of them `getfzs x,
0x225f`, `(x & 0xff) << 1`) and `_ufc_mk_keytab_r` 27 [lcc: objdump of
lcc 1.29.16's v5.8c2 sysroot] (found by the proof-of-concept back end,
I53).

Where lcc doesn't use `getf` and could:

- **Low masks wider than 32 bits**: `x & 0xffffffffff` is `andd` with a
  64-bit literal (two literal syllables of the four an instruction
  has); `getfd x, 0xa00` needs a 16-bit one (half a syllable), and
  `x & 0xffffffff` is `sxt 6, x` with none.
- **v5 masks with low zeros**: `(x >> 8) & 0xff0` is `shrd` + `andd`,
  `x & 0xfff0` an `andd` with a 32-bit literal; `getfzd` does each in
  one operation with a 16-bit descriptor. lcc keeps such masks as
  written even where it makes `getfz` of the same value written as a
  shifted field (above): `(x >> 3) & 0xff0` is `shrd` + `andd` where
  `((x >> 7) & 0xff) << 4` is `getfzd x, 0x8303`, `x & 0x7f80` an `andd`
  where `((x >> 7) & 0xff) << 7` is `getfzd x, 0xe3c0`, and `x & 0xfff0`
  an `andd` where `((x >> 4) & 0xfff) << 4` is `getfzd x, 0x8400` [lcc
  1.29.16 `-O3` for v5.8c2 and v6.2c3, lcc 1.31.05 for v5.8c2;
  `foldisa_getfz.c`].
- **Variable-length masks**: `x & ((1UL << n) − 1)` is four operations
  (`sxt`, `shld`, `subd`, `andd`); `shld n, 6` + `getfd x, t` are two.
- **Descriptors with bit 15 set as 32-bit literals**: `getf` ignores
  bits 16 and up (`getf.c` sets them in a register descriptor), so a
  descriptor with bit 15 set (BYTE 4–7, or 4–7 zero bits of `getfz`)
  can be written as a negative number, which gas puts in a
  sign-extended 16-bit literal (`getfzd x, -31997` is `_f16s 0x8303`)
  [binutils; hw for `getfd`, inferred for `getfz`]. lcc spends a 32-bit
  literal on each (the bit-field read above; 178 of Lua's 189 `getfz`).
  On v5 BYTE could also be 0, but forward-compatible v3 code needs it.

## Division [hw]

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `sdivd MIN, -1`, `sdivs MIN, -1` | MIN, no trap |
| negative dividend | truncates toward zero (−7 / 2 = −3) |
| `sdivd`, `udivd`, `sdivs` by zero | **SIGFPE, `si_code` `FPE_INTDIV`** |

Division by zero traps, so a compiler must not move a division where it
might not have been executed, unless it uses the speculative form
(`,sm`), which defers the fault into the result tag.

## Integer compares [hw]

Compares write a predicate. All of them evaluate `a − b` and test it
like x86 flags; `cmp<c>db` compares 64 bits, `cmp<c>sb` 32 bits:

| `c` | True when |
|---|---|
| `o` | signed overflow of a − b |
| `b` | a < b unsigned |
| `e` | a = b |
| `be` | a ≤ b unsigned |
| `s` | a − b is negative (sign bit), not "signed less" |
| `p` | the low byte of a − b has even parity |
| `l` | a < b signed |
| `le` | a ≤ b signed |

There are no `ne`, `gt`, `ge`, `a`, `ae` forms: swap the operands or use
the negated predicate (`~%predN`) in the consumer.

`cmpand<c>db` / `cmpand<c>sb` test `a & b` instead of `a − b`, with `c`
in `e` (zero), `s` (bit 63, or 31, set), `p` (the low byte has an even
number of bits set, x86's PF) and `le` (≤ 0 signed). lcc tests the flag
bits of a register FP compare with them (`cmpandesb r, 0x40, %pred`).

## Floating-point compares [hw]

**`UPSR.fsm`** (bit 8, "x86-compatible floating compare", user-writable)
changes the predicate compares for unordered operands: with it set,
`fcmpltdb`, `fcmpledb` and `fcmpeqdb` give **true** and `fcmpneqdb`
false for a NaN operand, as x86's `ucomisd` flags read by `jb`/`jbe`/`je`
would; ordered results, `fcmpuoddb`, the register forms
(`fcmpuddf`/`fcmpoddf`, 0x45 either way) and the exception flags don't
change (`tools/isa-probes/native.c`, 4C, 8C2, 2C3 alike). Processes
start with it clear, and lcc's startup sets it only to probe and puts it
back, so compiled code must keep it clear.

`fcmp<c>db` (double) and `fcmp<c>sb` (single) into a predicate, with `c`
in `eq`, `lt`, `le`, `uod` (unordered), `neq`, `nlt`, `nle`, `od`
(ordered). There is no `gt`/`ge`: swap the operands. With a NaN operand:

| Compares | Quiet NaN | Signalling NaN |
|---|---|---|
| `eq`, `neq`, `uod`, `od` | no exception | invalid |
| `lt`, `le`, `nlt`, `nle` | **invalid** | invalid |

So `lt`/`le` are the signalling compares IEEE 754 requires for C's `<`
and `<=`, and `eq`/`uod` are quiet. `neq`, `nlt`, `nle` are true for
unordered operands.

`fcmpud<d,s>f` and `fcmpod<d,s>f` compare into a register (32-bit
result; `d` double, `s` single operands) with x86's `ucomisd`/`comisd`
flag layout (ZF 0x40, PF 0x04, CF 0x01):

| a ? b | Result | Invalid flag, `ud` | Invalid flag, `od` |
|---|---|---|---|
| less | `0x01` | no | no |
| equal (also −0 = +0, inf = inf) | `0x40` | no | no |
| greater | `0x00` | no | no |
| unordered, quiet NaN | `0x45` | **no** | yes |
| unordered, signalling NaN | `0x45` | yes | yes |

`fcmp<c>d` and `fcmp<c>s` (same `c`) compare into a register: all ones
when true (64 bits, or the low 32 for `s`), else 0, with the exceptions
of the table above; they are x86 `cmpsd`/`cmpss` (`semx.c`, below).

`fcmpud*f` is the quiet compare that C's `isless` family needs; lcc
writes `isless (a, b)` as `fcmpuddf` then `r == 1` (`cmpesb`),
`isgreater` as `r == 0`, `islessequal` and `isgreaterequal` as two
`cmpesb` (`r == 1` or `0`, and `r == 0x40`) joined by `landp`;
`islessgreater` as the quiet predicate compares `fcmpoddb` and
`fcmpneqdb` joined by `andp`, `isunordered` as `fcmpuoddb`, and `long
double` with `fxcmpudxf`. `a < b || a > b` is two signalling
`fcmpltdb` [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`, v3 and v5]. **MCST's qemu raises
invalid for `fcmpud*f` on a quiet NaN** (it treats it like
`fcmpod*f`).

## FP min, max and combined operations [hw]

- `fmaxd a, b` / `fmind a, b` follow x86 `maxsd`/`minsd`, not C's
  `fmax`/`fmin`: if either operand is a NaN, or both are zeros, the result
  is **b**. (`fmaxd NaN, 1` = 1, `fmaxd 1, NaN` = NaN, `fmaxd 0, −0` =
  −0.) They implement `a > b ? a : b`, so a compiler may use them only
  where that is the source's semantics (or under `-ffinite-math-only`
  with no signed-zero concerns). lcc `-O3` (1.29.16 and 1.31.05) also
  uses them for `a >= b ? a : b` and `a <= b ? a : b`, which is wrong
  for signed zeros: `+0 >= −0 ? +0 : −0` gives −0 and
  `−0 <= +0 ? −0 : +0` gives +0, where `-O2` and below keep a compare
  and a select and give C's +0 and −0 [lcc, v3 and v5; hw: 4C, the two
  selects built at `-O3` and at `-O2`].
- **Combined operations** `X_Y a, b, c, dst` (gas operand order)
  compute **`Y(c, X(a, b))`**: the second stage takes `c` as its
  *first* operand. So `_sub` is **c − (a X b)** and `_rsub` is
  **(a X b) − c**, the reverse of what the names suggest:

  | Operation | Result |
  |---|---|
  | `fmul_addd` | (a × b) + c |
  | `fmul_subd` | c − (a × b) |
  | `fmul_rsubd` | (a × b) − c |
  | `fadd_subd`, `fsub_subd` | c − (a + b), c − (a − b) |

  The packed forms (`pf*_*`) apply the same rule lane by lane, with the
  packed stage operations `hadd(x, y)` = (x₀ + x₁, y₀ + y₁),
  `hsub(x, y)` = (x₀ − x₁, y₀ − y₁) and `addsub(x, y)` = (x₀ − y₀,
  x₁ + y₁) (low lane first): `pfmul_hadds a, b, c` = (c₀ + c₁,
  a₀b₀ + a₁b₁). All 63 combined FP operations of v3 (`f`/`pf` ×
  `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`hadd`/`hsub`/`addsub` × `add`/`sub`/`rsub`/
  `hadd`/`hsub`/`addsub`, `s`/`d`) follow it on the 4C and the
  Elbrus-8C2 (`tools/isa-probes/fcomb.c`, generated by
  `gen_fcomb.py`); the v5 `qpf*_*` family matches the community qemu
  (v5 operations, below), which builds every combined operation,
  integer ones included, as `op2(c, op1(a, b))`. The `f*_mul*` forms are
  v1 only.
- **Nothing special about them: a combined operation is two ordinary
  operations chained in one channel.** All 252 integer combined
  operations of v3 (`and`, `andn`, `or`, `orn`, `xor`, `xorn`, `add`,
  `sub`, `scl`, `scr`, `shl`, `shr`, `sar`, `getf` then `and` … `xorn`,
  `add`, `sub`, `rsub`, `s`/`d`; `merge_*`, which takes a predicate, not
  tried) give exactly what the two ordinary operations give run one
  after the other, `t = X a, b` then `Y c, t`, on the 4C and the
  Elbrus-8C2 over six input sets (`tools/isa-probes/icomb.c`, generated
  by `gen_icomb.py`). The encoding says the same [binutils, both qemus]:
  ALS opcode bits 0–4 hold **the first operation's own opcode** (`andd`
  0x01 makes `and_ord` 0x41, `getfd` 0x1f makes `getf_andd` 0x1f; for FP
  the opcode within the FP group, `faddd` 0x31 → 1, `fmuld` 0x39 → 9),
  and ALS bits 5–6 with the ALES group (`ICMB0`–`2`, `FCMB0`–`1`) hold
  **the second operation's opcode shifted right by one** (`and` 0, `or`
  2, `add` 8, `sub` 9; FP `add` 0, `sub` 1, `mul` 4). The second
  operation takes `c` as its first operand, so `sub` gives c − t, and
  the one slot that names no ordinary operation (6, `sxt`'s, for
  integers; 5 for FP) is `rsub`, t − c. The latency is the sum of the
  two (integer 1 + 1 = 2, FP 4 + 4 = 8, timing.md) and FP rounds after
  each stage (below); the integer forms run only in ALC1 and ALC4.
- `fmul_addd a, b, c, dst` = (a × b) + c with **two roundings** (not
  fused): `(1 + 2^-30)(1 − 2^-30) − 1` gives 0, not −2^-60. So a
  combined FP operation computes exactly what the separate multiply and
  add do, and a compiler may form one under any `-ffp-contract` setting
  (lcc 1.29.16 forms the same 95 `fmul_add` in a gemm at `-O3` with
  `-ffp-contract=off`), but never for `fma()`.

## Packed operations of v3 [hw]

`tools/isa-probes/semp.c` (generated by `gen_semp.py`) runs every v3
packed operation, 177 cases (the 64-bit packed integer and packed FP
operations, the immediate forms with six immediates each; not the
combined `pf*_*`, which `fcomb.c` covers, nor the tag operations) over
40 input sets on the 4C and the Elbrus-8C2, compared with both qemus
(as `sem5.c` does for v5). Everything matches the community qemu except
the points below, so its `target/e2k/helper_vec.c` describes the rest
(the proof-of-concept back end's finding I21, rechecked): lanes are
little-endian; compares give all-ones lanes; `pmerge a, b, m` takes b's
byte where m's byte is negative, else a's; `punpckl*` puts b's lanes at
even positions; `pack*` puts a's results in the high half; `pmaddh` is
x86 `pmaddwd` and `psadbw` its namesake; shifts take a count operand
(counts beyond the lane give 0, arithmetic shifts the sign). On v3 the
packed add, subtract, min, max, compare and average forms issue only in
ALC0/3, the multiplies, `pmaddh`, `psadbw`, `punpck*` and `pack*` only in
ALC1/4, shifts in either pair (binutils-ops.yaml), so 32-bit lanes rarely
beat six scalar channels. Where the hardware differs:

- **`pshufb` differs between v3 and v5.** Each byte of the third operand
  (the mask) picks a result byte: with bit 7 set, a constant (bits 5–6:
  0x00, 0x7f, 0x80, 0xff); otherwise bits 0–2 the byte and bit 3 the
  source (1: the first operand). On **v5** bits 4, 5, 6 then invert,
  bit-reverse and sign-replicate the picked byte (the community qemu's
  model; the 8C2 matches it in every byte); on **v3** they are ignored
  and the byte is copied as it is (the 4C, all 320 bytes). Both qemus
  apply the v5 rule to v3 too. A compiler targeting v3 must keep bits
  4–6 of plain selections clear (finding I21 took the v5 rule from
  qemu).
- **`psllql`, `psllqh`, `psrlql`, `psrlqh`** shift `src1:src2` (`src1`
  the high half) as one 128-bit value by **8 × imm** bits (bytes) and
  return its low (`l`) or high (`h`) half; the whole immediate counts,
  so 16 and more give 0 (both machines, every case). qemu shifts by
  `8 × imm` with a 64-bit TCG shift, which is undefined for counts of 64
  and more.
- **`pinsh src1, src2, imm`** inserts the low halfword of `src2` into
  halfword **imm & 3** of `src1` (gas warns about imm > 4; the hardware
  wraps, qemu leaves `src1` unchanged). **`pextrh src1, src2, imm`** gives
  halfword `imm` of `src1:src2` for imm ≤ 7; above 7 (gas: "undefined")
  the result differs between the 4C and the 8C2.
- **Some `pf` operations work on one lane** [hw: `semp.c`, all 40
  input sets on the 4C and the 8C2, the destination preset to
  0x5555…]: `pfdivs` divides the low singles and keeps the upper half,
  as `pfsqrts` does ("Square root and reciprocals"); `pfdtofs`,
  `pfdtois` and `pfdtoistr` convert the double to one 32-bit result and
  keep the upper half, `pfstofd` converts the low single to a double,
  and `pfdtoifd` rounds one double. Only `pfstoifs` of these rounds both
  singles. binutils gives them the matching operand sizes
  (`binutils-ops.yaml`: `pfdivs` sss, `pfdtofs` ds, `pfstofd` sd,
  `pfstoifs` and `pfdtoifd` ddd), and the community qemu computes them
  so.
- **NaN choice** in `pfhadds`/`pfhsubs` when both lanes are NaN: the
  hardware returns the low lane's NaN, qemu the high one's.
- **Flags.** Packed FP operations set the denormal flag (as the scalar
  ones do; no emulator does). The packed compares `pfcmpeq`, `pfcmpneq`,
  `pfcmpod`, `pfcmpuod` are quiet: no invalid for a quiet NaN (both qemus
  raise it); `lt`/`le` signal, as the scalar ones. **The packed divides
  and square roots `pfdivs`, `pfdivd`, `pfsqrts`, `pfsqrttd` never set an
  exception flag** on either machine (no invalid, divide by zero,
  overflow, underflow or inexact; the values are the IEEE ones), where
  the scalar `fdivs`/`fdivd`/`fsqrts` do: code that needs `fenv` flags
  must not use them.
- `puttagd`/`puttags` trap when asked for a diagnostic or pointer tag
  ("Tag operations" below). MCST's qemu gets `pfdivs` and `pfsqrts`
  wrong in every case.

## Square root and reciprocals [hw]

All in ALC5 only (the divider, timing.md). `tools/isa-probes/sqrt.c`
(generated by `gen_sqrt.py`; `check_sqrt.py` compares with exactly
rounded results on the host) on the 4C and the Elbrus-8C2, which agree
bit for bit; four rounding modes, about 4,000 random inputs each plus
special values:

- **`fsqrts`, `fdivs`, `fdivd`** are correctly rounded in every mode.
- **Double square root is two operations**, `fsqrtid x, t` then
  `fsqrttd x, t, r` [guide 10.4.2], and the pair is correctly rounded in
  every mode (0 of 16,040 results differ), with IEEE flags (invalid for
  a negative or a signalling NaN, which becomes quiet).
- **They give glibc's results**: `fsqrtid` + `fsqrttd` and `fsqrts`
  match MCST glibc's `sqrt` and `sqrtf` (called with every flag set, so
  its speculative code computes numbers) bit for bit in all four
  rounding modes, 605 operands a mode (special values, NaNs included,
  and random ones; `sqrt (-1.0)` is the default NaN 0xfff8000000000000
  both ways),
  and raise invalid exactly for a negative non-zero operand or a
  signalling NaN [hw: `tools/isa-probes/pocchk5.c` `sqrt`; 4C, 8C2 and
  2C3 alike]. So an inline root needs the libm call only for `errno`
  ([registers.md](../abi/registers.md), "MCST glibc's FP bugs").
- **`fsqrtid` is an intermediate in its own format**, not an
  approximation of √x: with x = m · 2^e (1 ≤ m < 2) it **keeps x's sign
  and exponent field** and replaces the significand by √(m · 2^(e mod
  2)) rounded to about 34 bits (low 18 significand bits zero; relative
  error ≤ 2^−34.6), so as a number it is √x · 2^⌈e/2⌉:
  `fsqrtid 2.0` = 2.828… (2√2), `fsqrtid 4.0` = 4.0. When the
  approximation rounds up to 2 the carry is dropped and the field reads
  1.0 (`fsqrtid 0x3fefffffffffffff` = `0x3fe0000000000000`). ±0, ±∞,
  NaNs and even negative numbers pass through unchanged (a signalling
  NaN is quieted); subnormal inputs get the smallest normal exponent;
  it raises **no flags**. `fsqrttd` halves the exponent, completes the
  significand and raises the flags.
- **`fsqrttd` needs exactly `fsqrtid`'s result**: it uses its second
  operand as the leading digits of the root, not as a seed it refines.
  Flipping one significand bit of it (bit 18, the lowest set one, or
  above) leaves the result wrong by about that bit's weight (at bit 18
  142 of 300 still right, above none), where one Newton step would
  correct a 2^−34 error. So a compiler must keep the pair together, and
  an emulator can compute `fsqrttd x, fsqrtid x` as the correctly
  rounded √x.
- **`frcps` and `frsqrts`** (single) are **12-bit approximations** of 1/x
  and 1/√x from a table: relative error ≤ 2^−11.6 in every mode, low 11
  significand bits zero (`frcps 1.0` = 0.99976, `frsqrts 2.0` = 0.70691);
  no flags ever; subnormal inputs give ±∞ (read as zero), ∞ gives 0,
  and `frsqrts` of a negative number gives a NaN without the invalid
  flag. They suit reciprocal and reciprocal-square-root estimates
  followed by Newton steps (`-ffast-math`); lcc never emits them, even
  with `-ffast` (`1.0f / sqrtf (x)` stays `fsqrts` + `fdivs`).
- **`pfsqrts` and `pfsqrttd` are not packed**: `pfsqrts` gives
  `fsqrts` of the low single and keeps the upper half (as every single
  operation does), and `pfsqrttd` gave `fsqrttd`'s results in every case
  tried.
- lcc emits `fsqrtid` + `fsqrttd` for `sqrt` and `fsqrts` for `sqrtf`,
  with a library call kept for `errno` unless `-ffast`. With `errno` it
  issues `fsqrtid,sm` on every path and `fcmpledb 0, x` into a predicate
  in the same or the next wide instruction, and calls `sqrt` when that
  test fails, taking the call's result as the root on that path
  ([control-transfer.md](control-transfer.md), "How lcc uses it"). In
  NPB EP's loop (`sqrt (-2.0 * log (t1) / t1)`) the call sits between
  `fsqrtid` and `fsqrttd,sm` (at `-O3` the next two points' loads
  follow it, beside `fsqrttd`) [lcc 1.29.16 `-O2` and `-O3`, v3, v5,
  v6]. For a negative operand nothing raises invalid before the call,
  which then traps in MCST's libm when `FE_INVALID` is clear
  ([registers.md](../abi/registers.md), "MCST's libm needs the sticky
  FP flags set").

## Other scalar operations [hw]

`tools/isa-probes/semx.c` (generated by `gen_semx.py`) runs the v3
scalar ALU operations no other probe checks, 172 cases (`merge_*` twice,
with its predicate false and true), and v4's `fscaled`/`fscales` on the
8C2, over 40 input sets (integers, doubles and floats: zero, normal,
infinite, quiet and signalling NaN, denormal; shift counts), recording
the destination and the `%pfpfr` flags. `check_semx.c` recomputes every
line on an x86 host: the FP operations with the SSE instruction named
below (taking its MXCSR flags, the same layout as `%pfpfr`), the integer
ones from the rules below. **All 6,880 lines of the 4C and 6,960 of the
Elbrus-8C2 match** (value, flags and signal); the two machines agree
except in the v4 operations the 4C lacks. So each rule below is exact on
those inputs.

`tools/isa-probes/tagx.c` (`model` section, `gen_tagx.py`) checks
`muls`, `muld`, `merges`, `merged`, `movts`, `movtd`, `movtq` and
`fstoistr` the same way, on semx's 40 sets, 140 edge pairs and 2,000
random inputs each, with `check_tagx.c` on an x86 host: **all 17,440
lines match on the 4C, the Elbrus-8C2 and the 2C3**, which print the
same lines. (`fstois`, `fdtois`, `fdtoistr` and `fadds` are also checked
by `fpenv.c`, below.)

| Operations | Result |
|---|---|
| `cmp<c>sb`, `cmpand<c>sb` | as the 64-bit forms (Integer compares) on the low 32 bits |
| `fcmp<c>sb` (predicate), `fcmp<c>s`, `fcmp<c>d` (register) | x86 `cmp<c>ss`/`cmp<c>sd`, `od` and `uod` being `cmpord`/`cmpunord`; exceptions as in "Floating-point compares" |
| `fsubs`, `fsubd`, `fmuls` | a − b, a × b, as `subss`/`subsd`/`mulss` |
| `fmaxs`, `fmins` | `maxss`/`minss`: b if either is a NaN or both are zeros, as `fmaxd` |
| `fstoid`, `fdtoid` | single or double → 64-bit integer in the current rounding mode (`cvtss2si`, `cvtsd2si`) |
| `fstoidtr`, `fdtoidtr`, `fdtoistr`, `fstoistr` | truncating single → 64-bit, double → 64-bit, double → 32-bit, single → 32-bit (`cvttss2si`, `cvttsd2si`; `fstoistr`: `tagx.c`) |
| `idtofs`, `idtofd`, `istofs`, `istofd` | 64-bit integer → single or double, 32-bit → single or double (`cvtsi2ss`, `cvtsi2sd`) |
| `fstofd`, `fdtofs` | single → double (exact), double → single (`cvtss2sd`, `cvtsd2ss`) |
| `fdtoifd a, b`, `fstoifs a, b` | **round b to an integral value**, a giving the mode as x86 `roundsd`/`roundss`' immediate: bits 0–1 the rounding mode, bit 2 "use `%pfpfr`'s", bit 3 suppresses inexact (also the `qp` forms of v5, below) |
| `fscaled a, b`, `fscales a, b` (v4+) | a × 2^b, b a signed 32-bit integer, rounded once, with IEEE flags (C's `ldexp`/`scalbn` in one operation) |
| `muls a, b`, `muld a, b` | the low 32 bits of the product of the low halves; the low 64 bits of the product (`tagx.c`) |
| `smulx a, b`, `umulx a, b` | the 64-bit product of two 32-bit operands, signed or unsigned |
| `sdivx a, b`, `udivx a, b` | 64-bit a ÷ 32-bit b, truncated, into 32 bits; **SIGFPE** when b = 0 or the quotient doesn't fit 32 bits (signed or unsigned) |
| `smodx a, b`, `umodx a, b` | the remainder of the same division (sign of a); SIGFPE when b = 0 or when a × 2^z, z the number of leading zeros of \|b\| as a 32-bit value, is 2^64 or more (unsigned) or outside [−2^64, 2^64) (signed) |
| `insfs a, b, c`, `insfd a, b, c` | rotate a right by b's bits 0–4 (`d`: 0–5), then replace its low *n* bits by c's, *n* = b's bits 6–10 (`d`: 6–11); higher bits of b are ignored (in `insfd` bits 13 and 15 choose tags [source: community qemu]) |
| `mpsadbh a, b` | four 16-bit sums: lane *i* = Σ\_j \|a.byte[i + j] − b.byte[j]\|, j = 0..3 (x86 `mpsadbw` on 64 bits) |
| `movts`, `movtd`, `movtq` | a copy (`movtq`: both registers of the pair); their tags: "Tag operations" (`tagx.c`) |
| `merge_<y> a, b, c, dst, pred` | y(c, merge(a, b, pred)): **a when the predicate is false**, b when true (as `merged`), then the combined operation's second stage, `rsub` included |

A conversion out of range or of a NaN gives x86's integer indefinite
(0x8000000000000000, 0x80000000) and invalid. FP flags include the
denormal flag for a denormal operand ("The denormal flag", below),
except in the conversions to an integer and the round-to-integral
operations (`fstoid`, `fstoidtr`, `fstoistr`, `fdtoid`, `fdtoidtr`,
`fdtoistr`, `fdtoifd`, `fstoifs`), which raise only inexact for a
denormal input, as x86's `cvt*2si` and `round*` do (semx's denormal set
on the 4C and the 8C2; `tagx.c` on all three). The modulo operations
are the odd ones: they trap
where their quotient wouldn't fit only through that leading-zero shift,
so `umodx 0xffffffffffffffff, 0x80000000` gives 0x7fffffff (a 33-bit
quotient) while `umodx 0xfedcba9876543210, 0x7fc00000` traps
(`tools/isa-probes/divx.c`: 894 dividend and divisor pairs around the
limit, the 4C and the 8C2 alike, all following the rule). A compiler
can use `udivx`/`sdivx` for a 64 ÷ 32 division whose quotient is known
to fit (x86's `div`), and a remainder only when it knows the dividend is
below 2^32 × b.

**Round to integral, every immediate** [hw: `tools/isa-probes/pocchk5.c`
`round`; 4C, 8C2 and 2C3 alike]. `fdtoifd`, `fstoifs` and `pfstoifs`
(both singles) ran with each immediate 0–15 in the four rounding modes
on 239 doubles and 238 singles: zeros, halves, ±0.49999…, values around
2^52 (2^23), subnormals, infinities, quiet and signalling NaNs, and 200
random values. All 45,760 results and flag sets a machine are what an
integer model of the roundings gives. Bits 0–1 choose nearest-even,
down, up or toward zero, unless bit 2 is set, which takes `%pfpfr`'s
mode instead. Bit 3 suppresses inexact and nothing else. Only a
signalling NaN raises invalid, and it comes back quiet; no other `FE_*`
flag is raised (the denormal flag: above). So `floor`, `ceil`, `trunc`
and `roundeven` without inexact are immediates 9, 0xa, 0xb and 8,
`nearbyint` is 0xc and `rint` is 4. lcc uses 1, 2, 3, 4 and 0xc for
`floor`, `ceil`, `trunc`, `rint` and `nearbyint`, so its first three
raise inexact, and calls `roundeven` [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`, v3 and v5];
MCST's libm does the same ([registers.md](../abi/registers.md), "MCST
glibc's FP bugs").

What lcc uses of these (its C library, libm and libstdc++ for v3, and
small tests at `-O3`): **`insfs`/`insfd` for bit-field stores**
(`p->y = v` for a 7-bit field at bit 5 is `insfs word, 0x1c5, v` then
`scls 5` to rotate the word back), about 2,800 times in those three
libraries; **`smulx`/`umulx` for `(long) a * b`** of two 32-bit values;
`fscales` for `scalbnf` on v4+, already at `-O2` and `-O3` without
`-ffast` (lcc 1.29.16 for v4.8c, v5.8c2 and v6.2c3; 1.31.05 for
v5.8c2), but never for `scalbn`, `ldexp` or `ldexpf`, which stay calls
even with `-ffast` or `-fno-math-errno`. It computes `int % int` as
`sdivs`, `muls`, `subs`, and `smodx` appears once in its C library, on
a sign-extended 32-bit dividend (where the limit can't be reached); it
never uses `sdivx`/`udivx`, `mpsadbh` or the flag operations below.

### x86 flag operations

A family meant for x86 binary translation computes an operation and
returns **the x86 EFLAGS it would set** instead of its value, in the
EFLAGS layout (CF 0x01, PF 0x04, AF 0x10, ZF 0x40, SF 0x80, OF 0x800)
as a 32-bit result; the suffix gives the x86 operand width (`_fb` 8,
`_fh` 16, `_fw` 32, `_fd` 64 bits; `s` operations have the first three,
`d` operations `_fd`):

| Operations | Flags |
|---|---|
| `adds_f*`, `subs_f*`, `addd_fd`, `subd_fd` | x86 `add`/`sub` of a and b: all six |
| `ands_f*`, `andns_f*`, `ors_f*`, `orns_f*`, `xors_f*`, `xorns_f*` and the `d` forms | ZF, SF, PF of the result; CF, OF, AF 0 (the `n` forms invert b first) |
| `incs_f* a, b, c`, `decs_f* a, b, c` and `_fd` | **a + b / a − b** (b is the step), with CF taken from c's bit 0 (the old flags, as x86 `inc`/`dec` keep CF) |
| `shls_f*`, `shrs_f*`, `sars_f*` `a, b, c` and `_fd` | count b modulo 32 (`s`) or 64 (`d`), as x86 masks it; count 0: c's flags unchanged. ZF, SF, PF from the low bits of the whole register shifted (so higher bits of a shift into an 8-bit result); CF the last bit shifted out of the operand of that width (zero- or sign-extended, so 0 or its sign once the count passes the width); OF as x86 for a count of 1, else 0; AF 0 |
| `scls_f*`, `scrs_f*` `a, b, c` and `_fd` | x86 `rol`/`ror` within the width: CF and OF (count 1 only, else 0) set, the other flags c's |
| `umulx_f*`, `smulx_f*` | CF = OF = 1 when bits *w* to 2*w* − 1 of the product of the 32-bit operands are not the zero (sign) extension of bits 0 to *w* − 1, as x86 `mul`/`imul` for *w*-bit operands; the rest 0 |
| `cctop<c> f` | predicate: x86 condition `c` evaluated on f's low 32 bits as EFLAGS (the upper half is ignored): `o` OF, `b` CF, `e` ZF, `be` CF\|ZF, `s` SF, `p` PF, `l` SF ≠ OF, `le` ZF \| (SF ≠ OF) |

Neither qemu implements the flag forms (both stop at them), and the
community qemu evaluates `cctopl` as true when SF and OF are both set.
lcc doesn't emit any of them for C: its `__builtin_add_overflow` on
`int` is ten operations of compares and selects (6 wide instructions
with the store and the return), and its `__builtin_mul_overflow`
divides the product by each operand, two `sdivs,sm` (`sdivd,sm` for
`long`) in 12 wide instructions [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3` for v3, v5 and v6,
1.31.05 for v6 and v7 alike], where `adds_fw` then `cctopo` give the
overflow predicate (`smulx_fw` a 32-bit multiply's, and `cmposb a, b`
alone subtraction's). A flag form's result reaches an integer operation
or `cctop` in its own cluster in 2 cycles and one in the other cluster
in 4, so the `cctop` in its own channel in 2 and the other `cctop` in
4. The multiplies' result reaches `cctop` or any integer operation in
6. `cctop*` reaches a predicated operation in 2 (1 on v6) and a `ct` in 3
(timing.md). `cctopo x` is bit 11 of x's low half for any register
value, so a compiler can model it as `(x & 0x800) != 0` [hw:
`tools/isa-probes/pocchk4.c` `cc`: 2^20 values per condition with
random upper halves, all eight conditions in ALC0 and ALC3, `cctopo,sm`
too; 4C, 8C2, 2C3]. The flags word is a 32-bit result: under `dbl = 0`
the destination's upper half is kept, under `dbl = 1` it is zeroed,
`smulx_fw` included [hw: `pocchk4.c` `dbl`]. With `,sm` the flag forms
and `cctop*` speculate like compares: a diagnostic operand gives a
diagnostic flags word or predicate, and without `,sm` it traps
([speculation.md](speculation.md); `tools/isa-probes/pocchk5.c` `dg`,
4C, 8C2, 2C3).

Apart from the flag forms, MCST's qemu differs from the hardware in this
sweep only in FP flags:
no denormal flag, invalid for a quiet NaN in the quiet compares (`eq`,
`neq`, `od`, `uod`), and inexact despite bit 3 in `fdtoifd`/`fstoifs`.

## 80-bit operations [hw]

`tools/isa-probes/semfx.c` (generated by `gen_semfx.py`) runs every
80-bit operation of v3 and the conversions and moves around it (88
operations, and v4's `fxscalesx` on the 8C2: `fx<op><b><r>` for `add`, `sub`, `rsub`, `mul`, `div` with a
second operand `b` and a result `r` single, double or 80-bit;
`fxcmp<c><b>b`/`f`; conversions; the square root steps), and lcc's
square root sequence `fxsqrti` → `fxsqrtu` → `fxsqrtt`, over 94 operand
sets (special values, random ones, and four that tell one rounding from
two) in six `%fpcr` settings (the four rounding modes at extended
precision, and double and single precision control). `check_semfx.c`
redoes each line with the host's x87. The 4C and the Elbrus-8C2 give
the same 51,324 lines (the 8C2 564 more for `fxscalesx`), and **every
line with an x87 counterpart matches x87 code in value and flags**
(43,992 lines on the 4C, 44,556 on the 8C2; the exception flags, not
C1, which is below):

- **Rounding as x87 code does**: the result is rounded to the precision
  control's precision, then to its own format. So `fxadddd` (80-bit +
  double → double) under extended precision gives what `fadd` then
  `fstp` to a double give, **rounding twice**: (1 + 2^−53) + 2^−80 gives
  1.0 where one rounding would give 1 + 2^−52 (538 lines tell the two
  apart, all the x87 way); under single precision control it rounds to
  single. lcc folds `(double) (x + d)` (x `long double`) into one
  `fxadddd` at `-O3`, also without `-ffast`, and that gives exactly its
  `-O0` sequence's result (`fdtofx`, `fxaddxx`, `fxtofd`), also checked
  on the 8C2 with the tie above.
- Operands of type `s` and `d` are converted exactly; an 80-bit result
  keeps 64 significand bits; the `s`/`d` results are IEEE values.
- **Compares**: `fxcmp<c><b>b` into a predicate follows the scalar
  rules (quiet `eq`, `neq`, `uod`, `od`; signalling `lt`, `le`, `nlt`,
  `nle`); `fxcmpud<b>f` / `fxcmpod<b>f` give the x86 flag layout of
  `fcmpud*f`, the `ud` form quiet and the `od` form signalling on a quiet
  NaN (`fucomi`/`fcomi`).
- **Conversions**: `fxtoid`, `fxtois` round in the current mode
  (`fistp`), `fxtoidtr`, `fxtoistr` truncate (`fisttp`), out of range
  gives the integer indefinite and invalid; `fxtofd`, `fxtofs`, `idtofx`,
  `istofx`, `fstofx`, `fdtofx` as x87 loads and stores. `movx` copies, `movxa`
  clears the sign (`fabs`), `movxc` flips it (`fchs`), NaNs included,
  without flags.
- **Square root**: lcc computes `sqrtl` (under `-ffast`; otherwise a
  call) as `fxsqrtixx a, t; fxsqrtuxx a, t, t; fxsqrttxx a, t, r`, and
  that chain equals x87 `fsqrt` in every line and mode (the `s` and `d`
  operand forms too). The steps alone have no x87 counterpart and are
  not decoded (as for `fsqrtid`, the intermediate is in its own format).
- **`fxscalesx a, b`** (v4+) is a × 2^b with b a signed 32-bit integer,
  but unlike x87 `fscale`, which is exact, it **rounds the result to the
  precision control** as an arithmetic operation does (62 of 564 lines,
  all under single or double precision control).
- **`fxdivt<a><r> src1, src2`** (`fxdivtss`, `fxdivtsx`, `fxdivtdd`,
  `fxdivtdx`) is src1 ÷ src2 with the **narrow operand first**: src1 is
  a single (`a` = `s`) or double (`d`) in the low bits of its register,
  src2 the 80-bit value, and the result a single, double or 80-bit
  value (`r`). `fxdiv<b><r>` has the 80-bit operand first; `t`
  presumably stands for this transposition (inferred). objdump prints
  the narrow src1 as `%drN` and, in the `s` forms, the 80-bit src2 as
  `%rN` (binutils' operand formats); gas takes either spelling. Both qemus
  implement it this way (MCST's `fp_helper.c`, the community's
  `helper_fpu.c`). On the 4C, 8C2 and 2C3, 16,512 lines
  [hw: `tools/isa-probes/sregs.c` `dt`: special and random operands
  under six `%fpcr` settings; `check_sregs.c`] give exactly the value of
  x87 code `fld src1; fld src2; fdivrp; fstp` to the result type,
  double rounding included (under single precision control `fxdivtdd`
  rounds to single, then to double). The flags agree too, except that
  C1 is never set for a single or double result (below), and that the
  conversion of src1 raises no denormal flag of its own: a denormal
  src1 divided by zero, a NaN or an invalid encoding gives no `de`,
  where x87's `flds`/`fldl` would set it (x87's `fdiv` itself would
  not). **lcc uses them** [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`, v3 and v5]: `1 / x`,
  `-1.0L / x` and `2.5L / x` (a constant exact as a single) become
  `fxdivtsx` of the constant as a single, which an `adds 0, c` puts in
  a register first (src1 takes no long literal, bundle.md; `0.1L / x`,
  not exact as a single, is an 80-bit constant and `fxdivxx`); `f / x`
  (`float` ÷ `long double`) becomes `fxdivtsx`, `d / x` `fxdivtdx`, and
  `(float) (f / x)` and `(double) (d / x)` one `fxdivtss` or
  `fxdivtdd`, whose double rounding is what C requires (at `-O0` lcc
  uses `fxdivxx`). Its v3 libraries use them 20 times
  (`lcc-usage.yaml`; libm's `atanl`, `remainderl`, `fmodl` and libgcc's
  `__powixf2` compute 1/x this way, `tanl` −1/x; the other 14 are in
  libgfortran and lcc's `libsanopt`). (`semfx.c` had passed the 80-bit
  value as src1, which made most results invalid; this section said so
  until 2026-10-12.)
- **`%fpsr.c1`** [hw: `tools/isa-probes/sregs.c` `c1` (8,920 lines),
  `dc` and `fp`, the same on the 4C, 8C2 and 2C3; `check_sregs.c`]:
  only a non-speculative divide or square root writes it. `fxdiv*` and
  `fxdivt*` with an 80-bit result, and lcc's square-root chain, set C1
  exactly when x87 does (the result was rounded up in magnitude, an
  overflow to infinity included) and clear it otherwise, exceptions
  included. With a single or double result (`fxdivxd`, `fxdivtss`,
  `fxdivtdd`) they always clear it. Their `,sm` forms never write it,
  also when they return the normal result (`fxdivtsx,sm` 1 / 3 with the
  flags already set leaves C1 as it was, where `fxdivtsx` sets it).
  Add, subtract, multiply, the conversions (`fxtofd`, `fxtoid`) and the
  compares never change C1. They neither set it where x87 would (175
  `fxaddxx` lines that round up) nor clear it where x87 would (an exact
  result, `fcomi`). Code that needs x87's C1 (an emulator; nothing a C
  compiler emits reads it) must compute it itself.

So the 80-bit operations implement x87 arithmetic exactly (C1 aside),
and a compiler can map `long double` operations one to one, including
an operation whose result is converted straight to `double` or `float`
or whose dividend is one (`fxdivt*`).
(MCST's qemu uses `%pfpfr` instead of `%fpcr`/`%fpsr` for them:
AGENTS.md, gotchas.)

## Predicate logic [hw, source]

A CLP (bundle.md, "PLS") combines two primary predicates `@pK`, each
optionally negated: `andp` and `landp` both give `c0 && c1`. The MLP
`movep c, v, @pD` with `pass @pD, %predN` writes v to `%predN` when c
is true and leaves `%predN` alone when c is false; a diagnostic c makes
`%predN` diagnostic (`preds.c` `mv_*`, 4C, 8C2, 2C3; guide 10.5.6 has
the operands the other way round; [predicates.md](predicates.md)).
`andp` and `landp` differ in diagnostic
(tagged) predicates, which a speculative compare of a diagnostic value
yields (speculation.md) (`tools/isa-probes/preds.c`, `lp_*`; 4C and
Elbrus-8C2 alike; a `ct` on the result traps with SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPN` if
it is diagnostic):

| Operation | first operand | second operand | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `landp` | false | diagnostic | **false, clean** |
| `landp` | true | diagnostic | diagnostic |
| `landp` | diagnostic | false or true | diagnostic |
| `andp` | false or true | diagnostic | diagnostic |

So only `landp`'s second operand is lazy, as C's `&&` is: a chain
`landp (landp (c1, c2), c3)` evaluates `c1 && c2 && c3` with each
condition computed speculatively under the ones before it, which is
how lcc merges a chain of branches into one (zlib's `longest_match`)
and how a loop combines an exit test with a second, speculative one.
Chains are limited to two levels in one instruction (bundle.md).

## Byte-swapped memory accesses (MAS bit 3) [hw]

The MAS byte of a load or store (`mas=N` in gas) is, for ordinary
accesses [source: kernel `asm/mas.h`, MCST qemu `mas-format.h`]: bits
0–2 `mod` (the access kind: speculation.md, atomics.md), **bit 3 `be`**,
bit 4 `m1`, bits 5–6 the cache hints (timing.md, "Memory"). `be` = 1
makes the access big-endian: the loaded bytes are reversed, then
zero-extended; a store writes its low bytes most significant first
(`tools/isa-probes/mas_be.c`, 4C and Elbrus-8C2 alike; memory holding
`01 02 … 10`):

| Access with `mas=0x8` | Result |
|---|---|
| `ldb` | 0x01 (one byte: nothing to swap) |
| `ldh`, `ldw`, `ldd` | 0x0102, 0x01020304, 0x0102030405060708 |
| `ldd,sm …, mas=0xb` (fully speculative, mod 3, + `be`) | 0x0102030405060708 |
| `sth`, `stw`, `std`, `stb` of 0x0102030405060708 | `07 08`, `05 06 07 08`, `01 02 … 08`, `08` |
| `ldqp`, `stqp` (v5) | all 16 bytes reversed |
| any of them at an address not aligned to its size (`ldh` +1, `ldw` +1/+2, `ldd` +3/+4, `sth` +1, `stw` +2, `std` +4) | **SIGBUS**, where the same access without `be` works |

A swapped load costs nothing extra: 64 dependent `ldd` take 309 cycles
with and without `be`, on both machines. Both qemus agree on the data
(`mas_be.c` at `-O3`, 4C and Elbrus-8C2 alike).

lcc folds a byte swap into the access only under **`-ffast`** (from
`-O2`; none of its component options alone does it), its set of
"potentially dangerous optimisations": the misaligned case above. At
`-O3` and `-O4`, `__builtin_bswap64 (*p)` is a plain `ldd` plus `pshufb`
with the mask 0x0001020304050607, `sa->sin_port = htons (port)` a 64-bit
mask literal (0x8080808080800001; 0x8080808000010203 for `htonl`),
`sxt`, `pshufb` and `sth`, and `ntohs`/`ntohl` loads add `sxt`,
`pshufb`, `sxt`; with `-ffast` each is one `ldh`/`ldw`/`ldd`/`sth`/`stw`
with `mas=0x8`. Its `__builtin_e2k_ld_*_be` / `st_*_be` builtins
(`e2kintrin.h`, 32, 64 and 128 bits) always use the bit. What the fold
buys (`mas_be.c` with `mas_be_loops.c`, both at `-O3`; same on the 4C
and the 8C2):

- **latency on a dependent load path**: 64 dependent `ldd` + `pshufb`
  (the swapped value used as the next address) take 629 cycles against
  309 with `mas=0x8`, 5 cycles a step (the shuffle plus the packed →
  integer crossing, timing.md). Scalar code that parses big-endian data
  sits on this path;
- **on the store side, instructions and a little latency**: 32 steps of
  swap, store and reload with `ldw mas=0x8` take 437 cycles through
  lcc's sequence and 421 with `stw mas=0x8` on the 4C, 501 and 425 on
  the 8C2 (the store-to-load round trip hides most of the swap); filling
  a `sockaddr_in` with a run-time port and address spends two of the
  four literal slots and four ALU operations on the swaps;
- **nothing in a pipelined loop**: lcc's sum and copy loops over 2,048
  elements in L1 run at the same speed either way (4C 1.49 ns, 8C2 0.78
  ns per element), the `pshufb` taking a free ALU slot and its latency
  only a stage; the MAS form is a few instructions shorter.

So a compiler should fold a byte swap into an adjacent load or store of
16 to 64 bits **when the access is known to be aligned to its size**
(GCC: `MEM_ALIGN` at least the mode's size; members of packed structures
and accesses through byte pointers don't qualify): never worse, 5 cycles
better on dependent load paths, two to four operations and a literal
fewer each time. (The array prefetch unit has its own `be` bit in
`mova`, apb.md.)

## Memory, tag and descriptor operations [hw]

`tools/isa-probes/semc.c` (generated by `gen_semc.py`) runs the v3–v5
memory, AAU, tag and protected-mode operations no other probe runs, 150
of them, each in its own child process from user mode, on a buffer of
known bytes; the 4C runs the 118 of v3 and v4, the Elbrus-8C2 all. What
user code gets:

| Operations | Result |
|---|---|
| `stq addr, off, src`, `ldq addr, off, dst` (v5) | store or load a register pair (16 bytes, low register first) at addr + off, **at any address** (v5 and v6; `memx.c` `q_*`). `ldq` takes ALC0+2 or 3+5, so two fit a wide instruction; `stq` takes ALC2+5, so one does |
| `ldqp`, `stqp` (v5) misaligned (+1, +4, +8) | v5 (the 8C2): **SIGBUS `BUS_ADRALN`**, `si_addr` the instruction, and `ldqp,sm` (mod 0 or 3) gives a wholly diagnostic value; v6 (the 2C3): they work at any address (`memx.c` `q_*`) |
| `ld… mas=0x7` (lock-wait) misaligned | SIGBUS `BUS_OBJERR`, nothing written (8-byte, all three; 16-byte `ldqp` lock-wait: `BUS_ADRALN` on v5, `BUS_OBJERR` on v6) ([atomics.md](../abi/atomics.md)) |
| `stmqp addr, mask, src` (v5) | masked 16-byte store: **byte i of the quad register is written when bit i of `mask`'s low 16 bits is set** (`0xaaaa` writes the odd bytes, bits 16–31 are ignored); the address is `addr` alone, no offset; on v5 **any address not aligned to 16 bytes is SIGBUS** (`BUS_ADRALN`), even with a mask that selects only the aligned part; v6 (the 2C3) takes any address and writes the selected bytes from there (`stmqp.c`) |
| `ldaab`, `ldaah`, `ldaaw`, `ldaad`, `ldaaq` (and `ldaaqp`, v5) | AAU loads: the element at the descriptor's base + `%aasti` index, where `staa*` would store it; served from L2, 9–13 cycles to a consumer, and with MAS mod 2 or 3 ordinary loads, not DAM checks (apb.md, "AAU loads") |
| `aaurr` (of `%aaind1`) | 0 |
| `aaurrq %aadN, dst` | the descriptor: after `aaurwq` of (0x0123456789abcdef, 0x10) the low half reads `0x1800456789abcdef`, the base's 48 bits with bits 59–60 set; the high half 0 on the 4C, `0x89abcdef` on the 8C2 |
| `gettags src, dst` | the tags of `src` (0 for an ordinary value) |
| `gettst` | leaves its destination unchanged |
| `invtc` | a value that differs between the 4C, the 8C2 and the 2C3 (not decoded) |
| `movtcd`, `movtcs`, `movtcq`, `movtrd`, `movtrs`, `movtrq`, `movtrcd`, `movtrcs`, `movtrcq` | copy the value (untagged operands; what they do to tags isn't visible to the ordinary store that reads the result back) |
| `gettc`, `puttc`, `puttst`, `getsap` | SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` |
| `getpl a, dst` into a register | SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPN` (its use is `getpl a, %ctprN`). This probe runs in a 64-bit process; in a 32-bit one `getpl` writes a procedure label: on v3–v5 the address with tag 0xA, on v6 a 128-bit label in an even register pair, an odd destination being SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` ([mode32.md](../abi/mode32.md)); in a protected one as well, with the module's index in the v6 label's high word ([protected-mode.md](../abi/protected-mode.md)) |
| `getva ap, off, dst` | the low 48 bits of the pointer plus off: (0x0123456789abcdef, 0x10) and 0x10 give 0x456789abcdff |
| `vfsi` | SIGBUS `BUS_ADRALN` |
| `aptoap`, `aptoapb`, `ldap*`, `stap*` | SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPN` (protected-mode descriptors; what they do in a protected process: [protected-mode.md](../abi/protected-mode.md), "Operations") |
| `cudtoap`, `gdtoap`, `ldgd*`, `stgd*`, `ldcud*` | SIGSEGV `SEGV_BNDERR` (the kernel's bounds trap) |
| `ldrd`, `strd`, `ldrqp`, `strqp` | SIGILL `ILL_PRVOPC` (privileged) |
| segment loads and stores `ld{c,d,e,f,g,s}s*`, `st{c,d,e,f,g,s}s*` (with `q`, `qp`, `mqp`) | a fault in every case, its kind (SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPN`, SIGSEGV, SIGBUS) varying with the operation and the machine: they use the segment registers a binary translator sets up |

So in user mode the useful ones are the AAU loads and descriptor reads,
`stq`, `stmqp` and the tag-free moves; everything that takes a
protected-mode descriptor, a segment or a privileged register faults.
`stmqp` suits vector tails, on v5 only at 16-byte aligned addresses (on
v6 at any); lcc's v5 and v6 byte loops don't use it. A vectorizer's
misaligned 16-byte access (`movmisalign`) is `ldq`/`stq` (or two `ldd`)
on v5 and `ldqp`/`stqp` on v6; a speculative `ldqp` on v5 must be known
16-byte aligned, or it is always diagnostic. Misaligned `ldq`/`stq` on
v5 cost more: 32 of them take 133 cycles for loads and 297 for stores at
+4 or +1, against 33 and 41 aligned or at +8 (v6: 33 and 41 at any
offset; `memx.c`). The tag
operations behave as plain moves on untagged data ("Tag operations"
below has what they do with tags); tagged values come from speculation
(speculation.md) and the protected mode, which this probe doesn't
cover.

### Tag operations [hw]

`tools/isa-probes/tagx.c` (generated by `gen_tagx.py`) runs `puttagd`,
`puttags` and (v5+) `puttagqp` with every tag operand 0–15 and some out
of range, on four values whose halves have bit 30 clear or set, plain,
`,sm` and predicated, then uses each result. The 4C, the Elbrus-8C2 and
the 2C3 print the same lines. A half tagged 1 is *empty* when its bit 30
is clear and *diagnostic* when it is set; tags 2 and 3 belong to
protected-mode pointers ([speculation.md](speculation.md), "Diagnostic
values").

| Operation | Tag operand | Result | Traps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `puttagd a, t, d` (ALC2, 5) | t's low 4 bits: bits 0–1 tag the low half, 2–3 the high half; higher bits are ignored (0x10, 0x100, 0x80000000 act as 0) | a with those tags (`gettagd` returns them) | **SIGILL `ILL_PRVOPC`** (the kernel's `priv_action`) when a half would become diagnostic (tag 1 with that half's bit 30 set), or would get tag 2 or 3 while the other half is not empty (tag 1, bit 30 clear) |
| `puttagd,sm` | the same | where the plain form traps, **a diagnostic doubleword**: a with bit 30 set in both halves, tag 5 (`0123456789abcdef` with tag 0xa → `41234567c9abcdef`); otherwise as the plain form (tag 5 on `0123456789abcdef` gives an empty value, not a diagnostic one) | none |
| `puttags a, t, d` (ALC2, 5) | t's low 2 bits | a's low 32 bits with that tag; the destination's upper half kept under `dbl = 0` (`ps_upper`) | SIGILL `ILL_PRVOPC` for tag 2 or 3, and for tag 1 when bit 30 of a is set |
| `puttags,sm` | the same | where the plain form traps, the low half with bit 30 set, tag 1 (`89abcdef` with tag 2 → `c9abcdef`) | none |
| `puttagqp a, t, d` (v5+; ALC0, 1, 3, 4) | t's low 8 bits, 2 per 32-bit word, the lowest word first | per word: tag 1 as asked with the bits unchanged (so diagnostic where the word's bit 30 is set, empty where it is clear: it never sets bit 30); tags 2 and 3 give tag 0 | none, `,sm` or not |
| any of them under a false predicate | | nothing written | none, whatever the tag (`pd_pfalse`, `ps_pfalse`, `pq_pfalse`); under a true predicate `puttagd` acts as the plain form (`pd_ptrue`) |

- The value operand is not checked: `puttagd a, 0` of a diagnostic a
  returns its bits with tag 0 and does not trap (`ld_put`, `pds_clr`;
  `puttags`: `ldw_puts`). The tag operand is checked as any operand is:
  a diagnostic one is SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPN` (`tagop_dg`); if its low bits
  also ask for a forbidden tag, `ILL_PRVOPC` is reported instead
  (`tagop`); with `,sm` the result is diagnostic (`tagop_sm`,
  `tagop_dgsm`).
- `gettagd a` returns a's two half tags (0–15), `gettags` the low
  half's (0–3), as a 32-bit result: the upper half is kept under
  `dbl = 0` (`gts_upper`, `gtd_upper`). Neither traps on a diagnostic
  operand (`ld_gettagd`, `ldw_gettags`).
- The tag-keeping moves keep different tags (`pd_movt*`): `movtq` keeps
  every tag, `movtd` keeps tags 1 and 2 and turns a tag-3 half into 0,
  `movts` keeps only tag 1.
- So in user mode a plain `puttagd` or `puttags` can only clear tags
  and make empty halves (`puttagd` also a pointer tag next to an empty
  half). A
  diagnostic value can be made on purpose with a `,sm` form
  (speculation.md, "Diagnostic values made on purpose"). MCST's qemu
  checks the tag operand of `puttag*` but not the result
  (`target/e2k/tcg/translate-al-c13.c`, `e2k_translate_prep_puttag`:
  "TODO: Implement proper operand checks") [source].

## The denormal flag [hw]

FP operations set `%pfpfr` bit 1 (`de`, denormal; no `FE_` name in
glibc) when an operand is denormal, as x86 does: `1 + 4.9e-324`
(`faddd`) gives flags 0x22 (denormal and inexact), `fmuld` and the
compare `fcmpltd` with a denormal operand 0x02, and `fadds` the same, on
the 4C and the Elbrus-8C2 alike; so do the v5 packed operations (below).
The conversions to an integer and round to integral don't, as on x86
("Other scalar operations").
Neither qemu ever sets it. Under `daz` (below) a denormal operand counts
as zero and sets no flag.

## Rounding modes, flush to zero and denormals are zero [hw]

`%pfpfr` has x86 MXCSR's layout (spec/abi/registers.md): flags 0–5,
**`daz` bit 6**, masks 7–12, rounding 13–14, **`fz` bit 15**. Both bits
are writable from user mode (`rws %pfpfr`) and behave as SSE's DAZ and
FTZ. `tools/isa-probes/fpenv.c` (`gen_fpenv.py`) runs every ordinary FP
operation (`faddd`, `fsubd`, `fmuld`, `fdivd`, the `fsqrtid` +
`fsqrttd` pair, `fmaxd`, the predicate compares, `fmul_addd`, their
single forms, every FP↔integer conversion, `fdtofs`, `fstofd`, the v3
packed `pfadds`, `pfsubs`, `pfmuls`, `pfaddd`, `pfmuld`; v6 `fmad`,
`fmas`) on 120 edge-case inputs under all 16 settings of rounding,
`fz` and `daz`, and on 1,500 random inputs in the four rounding modes;
`check_fpenv.c` recomputes every line with SSE under the same MXCSR on
an x86 host:

| Machine | Lines | Different from SSE (result or flags) |
|---|---|---|
| 4C | 245,520 | 0 |
| 8C2 | 245,520 | 0 |
| 2C3 | 261,360 | 32, all one case: v6 `fmad`/`fmas` with a = sNaN and b = qNaN return a quieted, x86's `vfmadd213` b |

So the ordinary FP unit is SSE plus MXCSR, bit for bit and flag for
flag, in every rounding mode and with flush to zero and denormals are
zero: `fz` flushes a tiny result after rounding and raises underflow
and inexact even when the denormal result would have been exact; `daz`
reads denormal operands as zero (with their sign) and suppresses the
denormal flag; `fmul_add*` rounds twice and the v6 `fma*` once in every
mode. Examples (all three machines):

```
fmuld 0.75*2^-1022 exact      %pfpfr 0x1f80: 000c000000000000 flags 00
                              fz     0x9f80: 0000000000000000 flags 30
fmuld 2^-540*2^-540, round up        0x5f80: 0000000000000001 flags 30
faddd denormal + 0             daz   0x1fc0: 0000000000000000 flags 00
fcmpeqd min denormal == 0      daz   0x1fc0: true
```

MCST's qemu differs in 2,232 lines besides its missing denormal flag:
with `fz` it raises no underflow or inexact when it flushes, `fmaxd`
under `daz` returns the denormal instead of 0, and for sNaN op qNaN it
returns the qNaN.

**Denormals cost one cycle, on multiplies only** (`fpcost.c`,
`gen_fpcost.py`; identical on the three machines): an `fmuld`, `fmuls`
or `pfmuls` whose operand is denormal or whose result is tiny has
latency 5 instead of 4; `daz` removes the operand case on the 4C and
8C2 (not on the 2C3), `fz` doesn't remove the tiny-result case. Adds,
subtracts and divides (`fdivd` 17 back to back) take the same time
with denormals. There is no microcode slow path as on x86.

## v5 operations [hw: Elbrus-8C2]

`tools/isa-probes/sem5.c` (generated by `gen_sem5.py`) runs every ALU
operation whose first ISA version is 5 (703 after leaving out loads,
stores and protected-mode operations: the 128-bit packed `qp*` family,
`plog`/`qplog` with all 256 tables, `addcd`/`subcd` with carry,
`getfz*`, `psrc*`, `pmullw` and others) over 40 sets of three 128-bit
inputs (integers, doubles and floats: zero, normal, infinite, quiet and
signalling NaN, denormal; shift counts), recording all 128 bits of the
result and the exception flags. On the 8C2 and under both emulators
(`-cpu elbrus-v5`):

- **Results**: all 703 operations give the same 128 bits on hardware
  and under the community qemu, so its implementations
  (`target/e2k/helper_*.c`, `fp_helper.c`) describe what they compute.
  MCST's qemu agrees except for `qpslld` and `qpsrld`: on hardware a
  count of 64 or more gives 0 (as x86 `psllq`/`psrlq`), MCST's qemu takes
  the count modulo 64.
- **Packed compares are quiet where the scalar ones are**: `qpfcmpeq*`,
  `qpfcmpneq*`, `qpfcmpod*` and `qpfcmpuod*` (both widths) raise no
  invalid on a quiet NaN; both emulators raise it (the same emulator
  error as for `fcmpud*f`, above). The `lt`/`le` forms signal, as the
  scalar ones do.
- **Round to integral** (`qpfdtoifd`, `qpfstoifs`; the first operand is
  the mode): bits 0–1 the rounding mode, bit 2 "use `%pfpfr`'s", and
  **bit 3 suppresses the inexact flag**, as in x86 `roundpd`'s immediate
  (every case with bit 3 set raised no inexact, every case without it
  did). MCST's qemu leaves bit 3 unimplemented ("TODO") and raises it.
- The denormal flag, above; otherwise the flags agree.
- No operation trapped (no SIGILL or SIGFPE with flags masked as the
  kernel leaves them).

So for v5 operations a compiler may take the community qemu's helpers
as the reference, minding the three points above. On the Elbrus-2C3
(v6) `sem5.c`, `semx.c`, `semfx.c`, `semp.c`, `sqrt.c`, `getf.c`,
`divx.c`, `fcomb.c` and `icomb.c` give the 8C2's output line for line
(about 195,000 lines), so v6 computes every v3–v5 operation the same way.

## v6 operations [hw: Elbrus-2C3]

`tools/isa-probes/sem6.c` (generated by `gen_sem6.py`) runs every ALU
operation whose first ISA version is 6 (67, without `ibranchd` and
`icalld`; the merges by a predicate twice, with it false and true) over
46 sets of three 128-bit inputs: `sem5.c`'s 40, four built from values
whose product plus addend differs when rounded once and twice, and two
with equal operands.
On the 2C3 and under the community qemu (`-cpu elbrus-v6`, the
`v6.16c` build). MCST's qemu's `-cpu elbrus-v6` is a 2C3 and runs the
`v6.2c3` build: its `clmul*` and `fma*` results match the 2C3's except
the denormal flag (which neither qemu sets, "The denormal flag"), and
it aborts on an assertion (`target/e2k/tcg/translate-lookahead.c:318`,
`op_descr->is_al`) at `mkfsw`, so the rest of `sem6.c` doesn't run
under it (`toolchains/sem6-mcst`, 2026-10-12):

| Operations | Result on the 2C3 |
|---|---|
| `fmas`, `fmad` a, b, c | a × b + c **rounded once**, as C `fma()` (`(1 + 2⁻⁵²)(1 − 2⁻⁵³) − 1` gives 2⁻⁵³ − 2⁻¹⁰⁵, not 0); `fmss`/`fmsd` a × b − c, `fnmas`/`fnmad` −(a × b) + c, `fnmss`/`fnmsd` −(a × b) − c; the single forms work on the low 32 bits. Every result matches Python's `math.fma` on all 176 double cases and the community qemu |
| `qpfmas`, `qpfmad`, `qpfmss`, `qpfmsd`, `qpfnma*`, `qpfnms*` | the same in every lane (`s`: four floats, `d`: two doubles), fused |
| `qpfmass`, `qpfmasd` | fused, adding c in even lanes (lane 0 is the low one) and subtracting it in odd ones; `qpfmsas`, `qpfmsad` the reverse. x86's `vfmaddsub` subtracts in even lanes, so it is `qpfmsa*` and `vfmsubadd` is `qpfmas*` |
| `clmull`, `clmulh` | the low and high 64 bits of the carry-less 128-bit product (x86 `pclmulqdq`) |
| `pcmp{eq,gt}{b,h,w,d}op`, `qpcmp…op` | a predicate: true if the compare holds in **any** lane (signed `gt`) |
| `pcmp…ap`, `qpcmp…ap` | true if it holds in **all** lanes |
| `pmrgp`, `qpmrgp` a, b, dst, pred | as `merged`: a when the predicate is false, b when true |
| `qpsrad` a, b | arithmetic right shift of both 64-bit lanes by b |
| `qpcext_0x00`, `_0x7f`, `_0x80`, `_0xff` a | 128 bits: a in the low half, the high half filled with the byte in the name |
| `qpchecks`, `qpcheckd`, `qpcheckq` a, b | nothing when a = b (32, 64 or 128 bits); SIGBUS `BUS_OBJERR` at the operation when they differ. The destination keeps its old value: an equality assertion in one operation |
| `mkfsw` a, b | an x87 status word: C0 = bit 0 (CF), C2 = bit 2 (PF), C3 = bit 6 (ZF) of a, TOP = b mod 8, every other bit 0. So a is an `fcmpud*f`-style flag result and the operation builds what `fnstsw` returns |
| `modbgv` a | 0; marks `%bgr` registers empty (a[7:0]) or full (a[15:8]) (loops.md, "v6") |
| `vfbgv` a, b | 0, or SIGFPE `FPE_FLTINV` when a register b[7:0] wants empty is full or one b[15:8] wants full is empty (with the initial `%bgr`, any b[7:0]) |

`mkfsw`, `modbgv` and `vfbgv` serve x87 code on the `%bgr` register
stack (loops.md); a C compiler has no use for them. Neither does it
for `qpcheck*`, except as a one-operation "trap unless equal".

Against the community qemu: the scalar FMAs, `clmul*`, the packed
compares, `pmrgp`/`qpmrgp`, `qpsrad` and `qpcext_*` match bit for bit
(the denormal flag aside); **its packed FMAs (`qpfma*`, `qpfms*`,
`qpfnma*`, `qpfnms*` and the `mas`/`msa` forms) are wrong**, giving other
values in most lanes; `mkfsw`, `modbgv`, `vfbgv` and `qpcheck*` are
unimplemented there (SIGILL).

The v3–v5 operations whose behaviour differs on the 2C3: `stmqp` takes
any address and `invtc` gives another value (above); the segment loads and
stores fault with other signals (`ldgs*`/`stgs*` with SIGSEGV
`SEGV_MAPERR` at a GS-based address); `srp` and `slrp` give SIGBUS
`BUS_OBJERR` (operations-v3.md); the v2 `tdtomp` encoding runs
without a trap (v3 and v5: SIGILL; v6 reuses the opcode).

## Other facts [guide]

- `%idr` (read with `rrd`, also in user mode; ready 2 cycles later, one
  read a cycle): CPU model in bits 0–7, revision 8–11, L2 write-back
  length 12–14 (2 = 64 bytes, `IDR_WBL_TO_BYTES`), core 15–19, node
  20–23, hardware virtualisation 24–28 (kernel `e2k_idr_t`). Models
  (kernel `bootinfo.h`): E2S (4C) 3, E8C 7, E1C+ 8, E8C2 9, E12C 0xa,
  E16C 0xb, E2C3 0xc, E8V7 0xe; 0 under virtualisation. MCST's qemu
  reads `0x2203` (`-cpu elbrus-v3`) and `0x2309` (`elbrus-v5`). Pinned
  to each CPU in turn [hw: `tools/isa-probes/sregs.c` `idr`]:

  | Machine | `%idr` | Fields | Linux CPU, NUMA node |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 4C (4 × E2S) | `0x2203` (CPU 0) … `0x31a203` (CPU 15) | model 3, rev 2, core 0–3, node 0–3 | CPU = 4 × node + core, node = node field |
  | 8C2 | `0x2309` … `0x3a309` | model 9, rev 3, core 0–7, node 0 | CPU = core |
  | 2C3 | `0x100210c`, `0x100a10c` | model 0xc, rev 1, core 0–1, node 0, `hw_virt` 1 | CPU = core |

  `sched_getcpu`, getcpu fast call 2 and the `getcpu` system call agree
  on every CPU. Cost in `%clkr` cycles per call in a loop, with the
  call: a function returning `rrd %idr` 14–15, the same as an empty
  function; fast call 2 53–59; glibc's `sched_getcpu` 88–98 (fast call
  2 behind glibc's wrapper); the system call 467–511. glibc never
  registers rseq on e2k (the port defines no `RSEQ_SIG`, so
  `__rseq_size` is 0 on all three machines). `%idr` is therefore a free
  hint for per-CPU data where a wrong guess only costs speed. It does
  not replace `sched_getcpu`: Linux numbers CPUs from its own
  enumeration (the interrupt controller's ids), `%idr` doesn't give the
  cores per node, and offline CPUs or a hypervisor would break the
  formula (inferred). lcc's `__builtin_cpu_is` uses its own model
  numbers ([source-compat.md](../abi/source-compat.md)).
- `getsp src2, dst`: src2 is a 32-bit signed operand; a negative value
  allocates that many bytes on the user stack, and dst receives the new
  stack pointer (guide 10.7.1; `getsp 0, dst` reads it).
- 80-bit operations (`fx*`): "80-bit operations" above; their registers
  and FP state: [registers.md](../abi/registers.md), "Extended parts and
  `long double`".
